summary: Parkevtate Vosianc frames the current AI capital-spending boom against the 1850s US railroad boom: railroads then were 3-6% of GDP, AI buildout now 1-1.5% and still rising. On that scale he picks five AI stocks he still calls undervalued in November 2026, valued on forward P/E, price-to-free-cash-flow, EV/EBITDA and his own discounted-cash-flow model. Nvidia at $218 versus a $345 fair value (about 58% upside over 12-18 months) is ranked his best stock overall; he owns it and may add before year-end. Micron at $929 versus $1,436 is sold out for all of 2027 and most of 2028, with free cash flow jumping from $2.61B in FY2025, though investors worry about what follows the shortage. Upstart at $24 versus $57 is the riskier pick, recently added, using AI instead of FICO scores for lending. IREN at about $27 versus $46 rents compute to hyperscalers with a growing backlog, but free cash flow is estimated negative through 2029. Broadcom at $342 versus $523 is called one of the best-managed businesses in the world; he owns it and wants more. Calls: NVDA, MU, UPST, IREN, AVGO all BUY reiterated, no flips.
